customFields.cdProgramDescr:
The department’s curriculum explores the dimensions of race, ethnicity, culture and identity, gender, and class in the United States, both historically and in contemporary times. Chicano and Latino Studies majors take courses offered in two broadly defined fields of study: humanities and social sciences. Humanities content includes courses designed to increase awareness of Chicana, Chicano, and Chicanx cultures, as well as intellectual, aesthetic, literary, historical, ethical, and human values. Social science content includes courses that analyze social institutions and how they affect the individual, as well as emphasize contemporary Chicana/o/x issues as they relate to the larger society. Areas of study include political science, anthropology, economics, sociology, and history. 

All courses in the Department of Chicano and Latino Studies are grounded in race, power, and justice. As an ethnic studies interdisciplinary field, this is our foundation. While other disciplines, such as history, English, or sociology, have individual scholars or subfields that are interested in these concepts, our discipline was founded on analyzing the world through this lens. Therefore, ethnic studies fields, such as ours, are leaders within the academy, offering some of the most innovative scholarship that addresses race, power, and justice. Additionally, community engagement is central to the origins and development of Chicano and Latino Studies. Many courses include community-engagement opportunities and support career options.

The Bachelor of Arts degree in Chicano and Latino Studies is designed to meet the needs of students preparing for careers serving Chicano, Chicana, Chicanx, Chicane, Latino, Latina, Latinx, and Latine constituencies and to prepare students for graduate and advanced professional study in programs in which a minority affairs focus would be an asset. The program allows students the flexibility of pursuing work in related fields, such as Latin American studies, Spanish, political science, African American studies, Women's studies, and American studies. Double majors are encouraged.

customFields.cdProgramLOsAssessment: CHLS engages with University-mandated annual assessment, evaluating three student learning outcomes (SLO) across three courses each year. We use our strategic plan which provides a roadmap for assessing student learning outcomes (SLO) across all courses on a regular schedule. The Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS) is responsible for conducting the annual assessment, reporting the findings and at the fall departmental retreat, and facilitating the discussion among faculty, instructors, and staff. Faculty implement changes in their syllabi based on the discussion and the report to improve student learning. As necessary, we discuss if the report requires revision of the curriculum as a whole (i.e. required classes and electives, when classes are offered, etc.)
customFields.cdProgramProgramReview: The department participates in the scheduled CLA Program Review, which includes external review for quality of program per CLA guidelines. The entire process informs department and college actions. The last academic program review was AY2018-2019, and it included a rigorous external review, discussions in the department with faculty and staff, and discussions with the CLA to determine future steps. We implemented several changes (i.e. new hires, new courses, community engagement policies and modules in multiple classes, programming, and staff changes). The chair leads the review and faculty and staff participate by gathering and assessing relevant data. Findings are reviewed by faculty and staff, and the CLA determines next steps for actions that require financial support. That is, actions that depend upon funds require CLA approval.
customFields.cdProgramLOsCommunicated:
To the public, once this review process is completed: On the Website.
To current students, faculty and staff: Coursedog.
To faculty and staff of CHLS: all of the above and the department annual fall meeting.

requirementLevels.label: Program Requirements
requirementLevels.notes:
All students must complete the University's Liberal Education requirements.

Collegiate Requirements:

  • All CLA BA degrees require 18 upper-division (3xxx-level or higher) credits outside the major designator. These credits must be taken in designators different from the major designator and cannot include courses that are cross-listed with the major designator. The major designator for the Chicano and Latino Studies BA is CHLS.

  • Students are required to complete 4 semester(s) of any second language, with a grade of C-, or better, or S, or demonstrate proficiency in the language(s) as defined by the department or college.

  • All incoming CLA first-year (freshmen) must complete the First-Year Experience course sequence.

  • All incoming CLA first-year (freshmen) students earning a BA, BS, or BIS degree must complete CLA 3002 or another approved career or internship course (CLA 3101, CLA 3201, CLA 3301, CLA 3896, CLA 3996, or CHLS 3896).

  • All students must complete a capstone in at least one CLA major. The requirements for double majors completing the capstone in a different CLA major will be clearly stated. Students must also complete all major requirements in both majors to allow the additional capstone to be waived. Students completing an additional degree must complete the Capstone in each degree area.

    At least 13 upper-division credits in the major must be taken at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities campus.

    Students may earn a BA or a minor in Chicano and Latino Studies, but not both.

rules.name: Electives
rules.description:
Students must take a minimum of 18 credits of Electives.
With prior approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies, up to 3 upper-division credits of courses not on the Electives list but related to the discipline may count towards the Electives requirement.

rules.name: Capstone
rules.description:
Take CHLS 4993W Senior Capstone (1 cr.) while also simultaneously being enrolled in a 3XXX or a 4XXX level course with a tenure-track faculty member in the Chicano and Latino Studies department. Alternatively, students may enroll in CHLS 4901W (3 cr.), if they have completed an upper division course in the major on the topic related to their capstone project. DUS approval required.

Students who double major in CLA and choose to complete the capstone requirement in their other CLA major may waive the Chicano and Latino Studies capstone, and they do not need to replace the 1 credit.
